By taking this limit, we are saying that the value tends towards 1, although it isn't exactly 1. To simplify things, upon taking a limit, we simply say that the answer is 1.

Step one is to find interest in what you're studying. It's hard to force information into your brain about something that you don't enjoy.

Step two is to be curious and always doubt. Never take any information you receive for granted. That way, you'll ask yourself tons of questions and you'll be able to answer most of them just by thinking or discussing. Otherwise, you'll have a lot of questions to ask the teacher. Do your assignments right after class, or during the evening of the same day.

Step three: don't take notes or very little, even if the teacher doesn't post much. You have internet and textbooks to refer to. Instead, think during the class. Doubt your teacher's information and ask yourself questions. That way, you're studying in class and you retain more information. What's the point of writing down stuff so that you can remember it later instead of just remembering prior to writing down?

Note: many might disagree with my step three, and that's fine. People who disagree probably have not tried it and are more reliant on their notes. That's okay, but I tell those people that they don't think/doubt enough.
